extraction.name: WebWalkerQA
extraction.description: A benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal, evaluating their capacity to traverse a website’s subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It contains 680 question-answer pairs across four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) and two languages (English and Chinese).
extraction.creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang
extraction.rai:dataCollection: The data collection process involves a two-stage funnel annotation strategy combining LLM-based and human annotation. First, official websites across four domains are traversed recursively to collect sub-links and pages. GPT-4o is then used to generate synthetic QA-pairs based on the gathered information. Finally, crowd-sourced human annotators conduct quality control, rewriting and calibrating questions and answers to ensure accuracy and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataCollectionType: Web Scraping, Software Collection, Manual Human Curator
extraction.rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains, specifically their HTML content and clickable sub-links.
extraction.rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: LLM-based filtering to verify and retain only legitimate queries with short answers containing entities. Human annotation to rewrite and calibrate questions and answers for correctness and consistency.
extraction.rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: A two-stage process: 1) GPT-4o performs initial annotation by generating synthetic QA-pairs from collected web page information. 2) Crowd-sourced human annotators perform quality control, filtering, and calibration of the synthetic queries to ensure they are correct, consistent, and reflect natural human-like phrasing.
extraction.rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset is designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to handle complex, multi-layered information on the web, addressing limitations of traditional search engines. It aims to improve RAG systems by enabling vertical exploration of web pages.
extraction.rai:dataBiases: The dataset is limited to four specific domains (conference, organization, education, game) and two languages (English and Chinese). It focuses on official websites with structured clickable content, potentially biasing towards authoritative sources and structured data rather than informal or unstructured web content.
extraction.rai:dataLimitations: The dataset size is relatively small (680 QA pairs) due to the complexity of query construction. It only utilizes HTML-DOM for parsing clickable buttons and does not include visual modalities like screenshots. The root URLs are provided, which may not reflect scenarios where the starting point is unknown. The dataset is static and does not account for dynamically updated information in real-time.
extraction.rai:dataUseCases: Training, Testing, Validation of LLMs and web agents for web traversal tasks. Evaluating the performance of RAG systems combined with web navigation agents.
